clinician.trajectory_summary: A 79-year-old female with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus (>18 years duration, HbA1c 17.85%) presented with acute onset right limb involuntary activities (dance-like movements) and somnolence for 1 day. On neurological examination, she had decreased muscle tension in right upper and lower limbs with characteristic dance-like movements, while left-sided motor function was normal. Laboratory workup revealed severe hyperglycemia (blood glucose 33.3 mmoL/L), glycosuria 4+, and negative urinary ketones, confirming a non-ketotic hyperglycemic state. Head CT ruled out acute stroke, hemorrhage, or tumor. Brain MRI on day 2 demonstrated characteristic ADC abnormalities in the left basal ganglia (ADC value 413×10⁻⁶ mm²/s) compared to normal contralateral side (857×10⁻⁶ mm²/s), with normal T1, T2, and DWI sequences. The patient was treated with intravenous insulin for glycemic control and haloperidol (5 mg intramuscularly daily for 3 days, then 2 mg orally twice daily). The dance-like movements gradually decreased after 3 days and completely resolved after 4 days of treatment, confirming the diagnosis of non-ketotic hyperglycemic chorea.
